name: Agulhas Return Current
scope: Source-scoped named-current extent from first clear evidence near 16 degrees E to loss of a recognizable jet between 66 and 70 degrees E. Does not include the subsequent South Indian Ocean Current or northern leakage branches.
layer: Hydrographic frontal/jet geography; study geostrophic velocities referenced to 1500 m. No velocity axis extracted here.
time_convention: Source combines cruises over roughly twenty years, mostly austral summer; CTD data 1983–1991. The sketch is not a simultaneous or climatological observed centerline.
source_locator: Printed p. 125, Section 3 paragraph before Figure 8: first clear evidence near 16 degrees E, meander near 25 degrees E, current progressively indistinct after 66 degrees E and absent in recognizable form by 70 degrees E. Printed p. 136, Conclusions: overall southward progression from 39 degrees 30 minutes S to 44 degrees 30 minutes S and separate naming downstream.
source_citation: Lutjeharms, J.R.E., and Ansorge, I.J. (2001), The Agulhas Return Current, Journal of Marine Systems 30, 115–138.
source_license: Copyright Elsevier 2001; factual geographic reference only; no paper figure or source geometry packaged.
coordinate_selection: OSW reference sketch constrained by the paper’s broad regional descriptions. Intermediate vertices are OSW-selected approximations, not published coordinates, a digitized source curve or observed streamline.
scenario_rule: Three OSW route shapes (nominal meander, reduced meander, amplified meander), three western-gate choices (16/18/20 degrees E), three eastern termination choices (66/68/70 degrees E), and independent endpoint latitude offsets (-0.5/0/+0.5 degrees): 243 finite scenarios. Eastern longitudes follow the source termination interval; western alternatives, latitude offsets and route shapes are OSW choices, not source error bars. Does not exhaust all actual meanders.
remaining_gates: Independent review of the source-defined western origin, eastern termination and source-specific flow identity.
Validate the editorial meander and regional waypoints against reproducible geographic or model geometry.
Canonical claim/measurement/geometry and atlas interface integration; retain source-specific scope.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW lesser meridional excursion near the Agulhas Plateau; not an observed alternate axis.
OSW greater northward plateau excursion; not an observed alternate axis.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 243 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
